etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English bemenen, bimenen, from Old English bemǣnan (“to bemoan, bewail, lament”); equivalent to be- (“about, concerning”) +‎ moan. Alteration of vowel from Middle to Modern English due to analogy with moan.
senses: (transitive, reflexive) To be dismayed or worried about (someone), particularly because of their situation or what has happened to them.
